author: cmungall
body:
Two paper-to-gene assignment errors put GABA-B receptor findings on GABA-A β subunit genes, affecting 30 SynGO records and the annotations derived from them. One gives the GABA-A β1 subunit a G-protein-coupled receptor activity (GO:0099528), which Ensembl has projected to 57 species, human GABRB1 (P18505) included; GO's inference then adds GO:0007186 to GABRB1.

- **Wrong gene.** Remove the 12 SynGO records on mouse Gabrb1 (P50571) from PMID:11498050, a GABA(B1) knockout. The same 12 records already exist, correctly, on mouse Gabbr1 (Q9WV18).
- **Wrong gene.** Re-curate the 18 SynGO records on rat Gabrb1 (P15431, 6) and Gabrb2 (P63138, 12) from PMID:15174078, an immunogold study of GABA(B1) and GABA(B2), against rat Gabbr1 (Q9Z0U4) and Gabbr2 (O88871). Please re-check each compartment and extension: the paper finds labelling in the main body of GABAergic synapses but mostly perisynaptic labelling at glutamatergic synapses.
- **Unsupported context.** Review GO:0099507 on human GABRB1 from PMID:26950270 (4 records: IDA, IDA, IMP, NAS): the paper shows channel activity of α1β1γ2L receptors in HEK 293T cells, not a presynaptic role. The channel activity is already annotated (GO:0022851, UniProt IMP, same paper).

Correcting the seeds may not remove every derived annotation: UniProt's GO_REF:0000120 rows merge several sources, and 4 UniProt ISS rows (GO_REF:0000024) copy rat Gabrb2's postsynaptic specialization membrane.

Full audit, record-level tables and methods:
https://claude.ai/artifact/39kJxHd2GTS1gJx6A7ETvh
title: GABA(A) and GABA(B) genes have been confused in annotations for a number of genes
